column1: # S-API-001: JSON API v2 requests replayed against the Canton 3.7.2 sandbox (the oracle) and against the Rust server.
# columns: id, method, path, body (JSON, `@file:<repo path>` for a binary body, or -), exact (JSON pointers whose VALUE must be equal, or -), bind (`name=/json/pointer;name2=...`)

# `{name}` in a path is the URL-encoded value bound by an earlier request; in a body it is inserted as is; the JSON string "@end" is replaced by the bound number {end}. Order matters: the requests run in sequence on one ledger.
# AT-T05 (S-TX-003): rollback scopes in one transaction on a participant, with key-diff.dar. A caught exception rolls back only its own scope;
# a rolled-back create never reaches the ledger or the transaction tree; an uncaught one fails the whole command. `/transaction/events/#` is the number of events.
# AT-U04 (S-API-016): the answers for an unknown, a malformed, an invisible and an archived contract id on the exercise path; the node must not tell
# a contract the actor cannot see from one that does not exist.
# AT-T03 (S-API-018): command deduplication on the node: the same command id of the same user and act-as set is refused while its period is open
# AT-L08 (S-LF-011): upgradable packages upg 1.0.0 and 2.0.0 (an optional field and other choice bodies in 2.0.0): which version a name reference resolves to and which body runs
# AT-U06 (S-API-020): active-contract filters on a party's view: by template (name reference, package id of each upgrade version), by interface with its view, wildcard, a union, and an empty one
# AT-U02 / AT-C06 (S-API-021): explicit disclosure. `tak` is neither signatory nor observer of an Offer but the controller of Take; the Offer is handed over as a disclosed contract
